chunk_findings.detail: The fold returned by `_load(repo, agent)` at line 196 is captured *before* `_sweep_finished(repo, cfg, log, st, …)` runs at line ~199, and that sweep writes the lease events it finalizes. The scan now reuses that pre‑sweep `State` (`state=loaded`) instead of re-folding the log as `L.scan(log, cfg, repo)` did before, so any event the sweep just appended is invisible to it. Concretely: run `brief` on a repo where an expired lease's item has just finished — the sweep appends the release/expiry event, and the recovery list is then computed from the renewal windows of a state that predates that event, so `brief` reports recovery/lease information that no longer matches the log it just wrote. The old code folded after the sweep and saw the new tail; to keep fold-once you must either sweep before `_load`, or have the sweep hand back the updated state / re-fold only the tail.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:239 (`L.scan(log, cfg, repo, state=loaded)`)

chunk_findings.detail: With the documented default the coalescing never fires. A renewal sets expiry = now + ttl, so between two consecutive heartbeats the expiry moves by exactly `lease.heartbeat_s` (default `300 s`), and the rule only suppresses a renewal when that move is ≤ `renew_log_min_s` (`120 s`). `300 > 120`, so every heartbeat is still logged. That is also what this repository's log says: 24 413 renewals in 13 active days across ~6 lanes is roughly one renewal every ~275 s per lane, still above 120 s. So under the default configuration the `lease.renewed` share stays at ~46% and the change's own acceptance criterion ("`lease.renewed` share under 10% of events") is not met for anyone who does not retune the knob — the default should exceed `heartbeat_s` (e.g. ≥ 900 s) or the comparison should be against a padded/committed expiry rather than the previous renewal.
chunk_findings.title: README.md (all-knobs table, `lease.renew_log_min_s` default `120`)

chunk_findings.detail: Before this change the view was built from one snapshot: `_load`'s state was discarded and `st = localize(fold(events, strict=False), log, time.time())` folded exactly the same `events` list that `PR.work`, `PR.detect`, `plan_for(..., events=events)`, `L.surface_contests` and `L.scan(..., state=st)` consume. After it, `st` comes from the fold `_load` performed on its own read of the log, while `events` is a second, later read (`log.read_all()` at the next line). Every consumer now combines an event list with a state that was folded at a different log position. Given the interleaving this change explicitly targets — six lanes polling plus heartbeats, i.e. another process appending `lease.renewed`/`claim`/`gate.passed` between `_load`'s fold and `log.read_all()` — the new event appears in `events` but not in `st`: `PR.detect(events, st, cfg)` sees a `gate.passed` just recorded by the other lane while `st.gates[gate]` still holds the failed record, and `plan_for`/`L.surface_contests` compute "ready"/"in flight" from a state that never saw the claim in `events`, so `ddflow status` renders a view mixing two log positions. The fold-once refactor should either pass the events it already read down (or fold `st` from this `events` list) so the state and the event list are the same snapshot.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/overview.py:112-114 (`_load(repo, agent)` + `events = log.read_all()`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new knob is only validated with `check=int_at_least(0)`, but its `doc` asserts a cross-field invariant that the check does not enforce and that is false for the values the check admits: "another clone sees this lease's expiry up to this much earlier than the holder's last heartbeat implies, so the window in force is never wider than heartbeat_s or grace_s ... raising this alone changes nothing." The coalescing rule (write a renewal only when the last *written* renewal is at least `renew_log_min_s` old) makes another clone's computed expiry lag the holder's true expiry by up to `renew_log_min_s + heartbeat_s`, so the divergence is bounded by `renew_log_min_s`, not by `heartbeat_s`/`grace_s`. With the permitted configuration `renew_log_min_s = 7200, heartbeat_s = 300, ttl_s = 1800, grace_s = 120`, an agent that is alive and renewing every 300 s still has its last *logged* renewal up to ~7500 s old; another clone on the same NFS checkout computes `last_written + ttl_s + grace_s` and reports the lease reclaimable for ~5400 s stretches, so a second agent can claim and edit the same worktree while the first is running. This is exactly the invariant the reorganisation caution requires to be proved by a two-clone test ("keeping heartbeats only in .ddflow/local is allowed ONLY if the expiry another clone computes is unchanged within grace_s"); the knob needs an upper bound relative to `ttl_s`/`grace_s` (or the handler must clamp the skipped window), and the doc's "raising this alone changes nothing" is what invites an operator into this state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/lease.py `renew_log_min_s`

chunk_findings.detail: The guard tests `it.lease_contest or it.displaced` **before** the `_widen` that the rest of the function (and the file's own comment) exists to perform, and the widening is itself what creates an overlap that the guard is asking about. Concretely: lease A holds item X with window `[t0, t0+W]` and is uncontested. A renews at `t1` (`t0 < t1`), which under the old code widened A's displayed claim to `[.., t1+W]` in the folded state before `_clashing`/`_join`. A rival claim B is then processed at `t2` with `t0+W < t2 < t1+W`. In the old fold, A's stored window already covered `t2`, so B's claim clashed, the two windows joined, and the item became contested. Under the new guard A is not yet contested or displaced at `t1` (that is precisely why it used to be widened), so `_widen` is skipped, A's known window stays `[t0, t0+W]`, and B's claim at `t2` no longer clashes at all: no `_join`, no contested flag, and any rendering of the claim window shows the old end. The justification in the comment ("the displayed claim never clashes with itself") only rules out self-overlap; the widening is not for self-clash, it is what makes later, not-yet-seen rivals (`_clashing(_known(it), ...)`) visible, so the "nothing to widen and nothing to meet" claim is false. Because the fold accumulates state, this changes the folded `State` for any log where a lease is renewed beyond its original window and a later claim lands inside the extension, violating the stated "byte-identical fold output on this log / replay-equivalence for status, next, board, lease expiry" acceptance criterion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/leases.py:226 (_late_renewal)

chunk_findings.detail:
`_positions()` caches `id -> index` and rebuilds only when `len(table) != len(self.items)`. The membership test in `next` is done against that cached table (`if n in pos`) while the value is fetched from `self.items` (`self.items[n]`), so the two containers are assumed to be in lockstep. Any change that keeps the item count the same but alters the key set leaves the table stale, and the failure is not benign:

- a stale id `X` that is still in `pos` but no longer a key of `self.items` makes `self.items["X"]` raise `KeyError` out of `next(phase)`;
- a new id `Y` that is a descendant of `phase` but absent from `pos` is silently dropped (`if n in pos` is False), so `ddflow next --phase ...` returns an incomplete task list with no error.

Trigger: a single fold that removes one item key and inserts another (e.g. any rekey/replace/supersede step, or a state rebuild that reconstructs `items` with the same number of keys in a different order), followed by `next(phase)` on the same `State`. The comment "Items are only ever added (a removal sets a flag), so a table of this length is still right" justifies the length check only for flag-based removals; the cache itself enforces nothing, and it is not keyed on the identity/keys of `items`. Note the class already has the same latent hazard via `_child_index` (which feeds `descendants`), so a stale table can be paired with a stale child index. Rebuilding when `items` is not the same object the table was built from (or checking `n in self.items` instead of `in pos`) avoids both the KeyError and the silent omission.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/records.py: `State._positions` / `State.next`

chunk_findings.detail: The module and class docstrings state the invariant "Every file operation goes through `fsio`, and the class is the only thing callers touch, so a different backend (the planned storage seam, D-storage) replaces it without touching a caller." The write path honours this (`fsio.atomic_write`), but the read, list and delete paths do not: `get_bytes` calls `path.read_bytes()` (blobstore.py:56-62), `refs` calls `self.dir.is_dir()` / `self.dir.glob("??/*.json")`, and `remove` calls `path.unlink()` (blobstore.py:71-75). Concretely, if the storage seam is exercised (a backend that is not the local filesystem — exactly what the docstring says the class is designed to allow), then `BlobStore(root).get_bytes(ref)` and `.remove(ref)` keep hitting `root/.ddflow/blobs/...` directly and will silently return `None` / no-op instead of consulting the backend, so a blob written through the backend cannot be read back or deleted and folds that re-fetch a blob would treat it as missing (the `put` existence check in line 51 also goes through this unverified read). Either route these three operations through `fsio` like the write path, or drop the claim that the seam is transparent for all file operations.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/blobstore.py — `BlobStore.get_bytes` / `refs` / `remove`

chunk_findings.detail: `_shard_meta()` promises in its own docstring to return `None` "where no cache is kept (`[log].snapshot` off, **a log built only to read another repository**)", but the body only tests `self._snapshot_enabled()` and never consults `self.cache_writes` — the flag the constructor documents as meaning "reading it must not leave a snapshot in it" (the B244aeaad5c invariant the surrounding `__init__` is careful to preserve, deriving the clone id on first use rather than in the constructor). Everywhere else a snapshot is persisted, that flag is the write guard; here the new mechanism writes through a different path (`SMT.ShardMeta(self.root)` / `meta.facts(...)` inside `_stamp_events`), so the guard is bypassed. Concretely: build an `EventLog` for a repository that is only being read (the export / sibling-worktree case the class comment names, i.e. `cache_writes=False`) with `[log].snapshot` left at its enabled default, then let the version/skew guard evaluate (`stamp_facts(self._stamp_events(), ...)`); `_shard_meta()` returns a `ShardMeta` rather than `None`, and the first `facts()`/`ShardMeta` construction persists or updates the per-clone sidecar under the examined repository's `.ddflow/local`, mutating a log this instance was explicitly told not to write snapshots into. The check should be `if not self._snapshot_enabled() or not self.cache_writes: return None` (or `_snapshot_enabled()` must itself fold in `cache_writes`); as written the stated contract and the B244aeaad5c guard are not met.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log.py:1141 (`EventLog._shard_meta`)

chunk_findings.detail: `advance` verifies only that the cached row described the shard *before* the append (`(row.size, row.mtime_ns) != before` → bail), and then, without any further check, records the shard's **current** `(st_size, st_mtime_ns)` as the identity of a record whose contents are asserted to be `row + ev`: `high = max(int(row["high"]), ev.lamport)` and `stamps = [*row["stamps"], *ev]`. Nothing verifies that the file now holds exactly the pre-append content plus that one event (a cheap check would be `stamp[0] == before[0] + len(line)` where `line` is the appended JSON, plus a matching mtime change). Consequently any write to that shard which this clone's append lock does not serialise and which lands in the window between the append and `self._stamp(shard)` is laundered into a record that matches the file's on-disk stat. Concretely: process A (holding the local append lock) appends event E to `.ddflow/events/<shard>.jsonl`, and a `git merge`/`git pull` — the two-clone merge scenario the module docstring and the acceptance criteria explicitly name — rewrites that shard with the other clone's events before A calls `advance`. A writes `{size: <post-merge size>, mtime_ns: <post-merge mtime>, high: max(old_high, E.lamport), stamps: old_stamps + E}`. `_current` then accepts this record forever (size and mtime match), so the next write computes its Lamport from a `high` that omits the merged events — e.g. the shard holds `[1,2,3,4,2]` (the docstring's own example) while the cache still says `high=2`, so the next append re-uses Lamport 3 and collides with an existing event. The same stale record makes `facts` return a `stamps` list missing merged `skew.overridden` / `session.*` / `ddflow.capabilities` facts, so the version/skew guard folds as if the other clone's override never happened. The same hole is reachable without any concurrency if a caller appends several events and calls `advance` once with the pre-batch `before`: the record then covers only the last event's high and stam
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/shardmeta.py:103 (`ShardMeta.advance`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch returns `True` ("renewed") for a lease whose renewal is *not* written to the log, and the suppression window is taken verbatim from config (`renew_window(Config.load(log.root))` at line ~553) with nothing in this change bounding it by `cfg.lease.grace_s`. The only lease-age evidence any other process/clone has is the last *logged* `lease.renewed`; every folded view therefore now lags the holder's real expiry by up to `renew_log_min_s`. That break reaches two consumers that the task's own reorganisation audit (caution 2, "core/handlers/leases.py (`_late_renewal`, the pairwise lease-window logic) uses the last renewal to widen a lease window ... allowed ONLY if the expiry another clone computes is unchanged within grace_s") calls out, and one in this very file: `scan` line ~861 does `state.active_leases(now, cfg.lease.grace_s)` on the same fold, and `lapsed_onto_a_live_claim` (the `refuse` passed at the renew call site) compares liveness from that fold. Concretely: with `[lease] renew_log_min_s = 120, grace_s = 30` and a holder renewing every 60 s, a fold taken mid-window reports an expiry 0–120 s behind reality; a renewal that arrives on the far side of the stale pair-wise window is judged late/out-of-window by `_late_renewal` and by `active_leases(now, grace_s)`, i.e. the holder is treated as expired while it is actively renewing. Since `renew_log_min_s` and `grace_s` are independently settable knobs (config_sections/log.py) and no clamp or cross-validation is added here, this is reachable by configuration alone; the diff should either clamp the quiet window to the grace band or make the quiet decision evaluate the *unwidened* expiry another clone will compute.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:521 (`_append_lease_event` quiet branch)

chunk_findings.detail:
`renew_window` returns `min(renew_log_min_s, heartbeat_s, grace_s)`, so the window it hands to `quiet_renewal` is *never wider than one heartbeat interval*. `quiet_renewal` suppresses only when `0 <= now - lease.renewed_at < min_s`, and `renewed_at` is the last **written** renewal, so the age it compares against is at least one heartbeat interval (the next heartbeat comes at `renewed_at + heartbeat_s` or later). With `age >= heartbeat_s >= min_s`, `age < min_s` is false at every heartbeat, so no renewal is ever suppressed: coalescing only ever fires for renewals emitted *more often* than `heartbeat_s`, i.e. never for the cadence the module's own docstring assumes ("a project that heartbeats every second has asked to see each one").

Concrete case: `[lease] heartbeat_s = 30, renew_log_min_s = 600, grace_s = 300`. `renew_window` returns 30. A holder heartbeating every 30 s produces attempts with `age = 30, 60, …` measured from the last written renewal; the first attempt after each write has `age = 30 >= 30`, so every `lease.renewed` is written and the renewal share stays at the measured 46 %, making the acceptance target ("`lease.renewed` under 10 % of events") unreachable. The intent and the reorganisation caution bound the window by `renew_log_min_s` and `grace_s` only; the `heartbeat_s` term inverts the intended semantics (the smaller the configured heartbeat interval, the stronger the coalescing should be, not weaker).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/logcoalesce.py:24 (`renew_window`)

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture intends to emit `gate.started` events, but under its own default it never can. `GATES = ("research", "rules", "implement", "rubber_duck", "critic", "standards", "ci", "unit_tests")`, and gates are only drawn on odd heartbeat indices: `for i in range(beats)` with `beats=13` visits `i ∈ {1,3,5,7,9,11}`, i.e. exactly six `gates.pop(0)` calls, which consume only indices 0–5 (`research … standards`). The command gates that the code specifically checks for — `if g in ("ci", "unit_tests"): w.add(agent, "gate.started", ...)` — sit at indices 6 and 7 and are therefore never reached. So for any generated log (e.g. `generate(tmp/"events", 565_000)` with defaults), no `gate.started` event is written at all: the branch is dead, the per-kind byte/count mix the fixture is used to measure silently omits a whole event kind, and any test that uses this fixture to exercise `gate.started` handling passes vacuously while covering nothing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/logfixture.py:generate / GATES

chunk_findings.detail: Given `--events <clone>/.ddflow/events` from a repository whose log references content-addressed evidence blobs, the scratch project has no `.ddflow/blobs/` directory, so every command that resolves evidence (doctor/verify, and depending on the renderer status/brief) fails with a missing-blob error. `main()` then prints a `wall_s`/`cpu_s` row for that run anyway — the number is process start plus the failure, not a read of the log — and the only signal is `"exit"`, so a before/after table built from these runs for exactly the case under test (the real 35 MB log) is silently wrong. The `--synth --modern` path does create blobs, so generated workloads and copied real logs are not comparable. Fix: copy/link the sibling `.ddflow/blobs` store alongside the events directory (and fail loudly if a referenced blob hash is dangling) before timing any command.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/logbench.py:33-35 (`project`)

chunk_findings.detail: The test counts fold work by monkeypatching `records.State.__init__` and asserts an exact `== 1`, but that counts *constructor calls*, not folds, and the warm-up `_run(project, *cmd)` plus the measured `_folds(...)` run in the same process against the same unchanged log. An implementation that caches the folded State per log digest — explicitly permitted by the task text ("a per-process memo keyed by the log digest is acceptable only if the State is not mutated") — will hit the memo on the measured run, construct zero `State`s, and the assertion at line 55 (`== 1`) fails even though the command behaves exactly as required (same output, one actual fold). Conversely, the natural way to make the State pure after `localize` mutates it — copying via `dataclasses.replace` — calls `__init__`, inflating the count above 1 and failing the same assertion for a correct implementation. `test_brief_folds_at_most_twice` has the same `1 <= ...` dependence on the in-process count and fails the same way (0 folds under the memo). So the test both false-fails a permitted implementation and cannot distinguish "folded once" from "constructed once": the assertion should be driven by a fold counter (or by asserting the observable answers equal a from-scratch multi-fold baseline), not by the number of `State.__init__` invocations in the process.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_fold_once.py:41-55 (`_folds` / `test_a_read_command_folds_the_log_once`)

chunk_findings.detail: The autouse fixture clears `BS._KNOWN_ROOTS` to make the suite pass, and its own docstring states the production behaviour it is hiding: "Blobs are found by hash in every project the process opened; another test's identical blob would answer for a removed one." That means the blob reader resolves a reference by scanning *every* root the process has registered, not the root of the log being read. Concretely: one ddflow process opens clone A and clone B (exactly the two-clone case the intent names in `HOW TO TEST`); both hold the same content-addressed gate-evidence blob; delete (or overwrite) A's copy under `.ddflow/blobs/`. Reading A's `gate.failed` event still returns the correct value from B, so `LB.full` never yields `B.Unavailable` and `LB.problems`/doctor never report the missing or tampered blob in A. `test_a_missing_blob_is_unavailable_never_empty` and `test_a_tampered_blob_is_detected` only observe the intended behaviour because the fixture wipes the registry first, so the guarantee the intent states ("a blob that cannot be read is reported, never taken for empty", "blob tamper detected by doctor", "tamper-evidence unchanged") is not actually tested or held for the multi-project process. The fix is to look the blob up under the root of the event/log being read (or to make the global fast path hash-verified per root) rather than clearing the registry in the fixture.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_log_blobs.py:22-29 (`_only_this_tests_projects`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change's own pinning test documents that the stated acceptance target is unreachable at the shipped default. ACCEPTANCE says "lease.renewed share under 10% of events on the generated workload", but this test hardcodes `coalesced(events, 300)` — a 300 s window, not the default — and only asserts `after / len(small) < 0.25 < before / len(events)`. Its docstring then states outright: "The share stays above 10% at the default window (120 s, = grace_s): an item's life is hours of heartbeats, and bounding the drift by grace_s bounds the saving." With the heartbeat pace used here (one beat every 20 s) and a 120 s window, one renewal is written every ~120 s instead of every 300 s, so the post-coalescing renewal share lands just above 10% (≈11% of the thinned event stream) rather than "under 10%": the acceptance criterion is met only by passing a non-default window, and the test masks the shortfall by asserting <25%. The test should either assert the acceptance number at the default window (in which case it fails), or the default `renew_log_min_s`/window logic must be changed so the criterion holds as shipped. As written, the test passes while the documented acceptance does not.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_log_scale.py::test_a_busy_workload_writes_a_fifth_of_its_renewals_and_a_fraction_of_the_events
